# Actuo

> An expense management platform where every meaningful action is also a WebMCP
> tool, so an AI agent can operate the app on a user's behalf transparently and
> within the same permission boundaries as a human.

Actuo is BYOK: it never holds or proxies an LLM key. Each user supplies their own
Google Gemini API key, it is stored only in their browser, and every model call
goes directly from the browser to Google.

## Tools exposed via WebMCP

Registered on `document.modelContext` once a user is signed in:

- `search_expenses` — search the organization's expenses by text, status or date
  range. Read-only.
- `submit_expense` — create an expense and submit it for approval. Mutating;
  requires explicit user confirmation before it runs.
- `get_budget_status` — per-category budget, spend, remaining and utilization.
  Read-only.
- `generate_report` — generate a CSV expense report for a date range.
  Long-running and cancellable via AbortSignal.
- `approve_expense` — approve or reject a submitted expense. Registered only
  while the signed-in user is an admin or owner AND items are pending, so it
  appears and disappears with `toolchange`. Mutating; requires confirmation.

The Add Expense page additionally exposes a *declarative* tool: the form is
annotated plain HTML (`toolname`, `tooldescription`, `toolparamdescription`,
`toolautosubmit`) with no JavaScript tool registration at all.

## Permissions

An agent can do exactly what the signed-in user can do, and nothing more. Roles
(`owner`, `admin`, `member`) are enforced server-side on every request, so a tool
call is authorized the same way a click is. Every invocation, by a human or an
agent, is written to an audit log.

## Notes for agents

- WebMCP is behind a flag in current Chrome: `chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing`.
- Amounts may be filed in several currencies; `convertedAmount` is the value in
  the organization's base currency and is what totals should use.
